catchRubric:
# What review caught on a light-routed change — coding rubric (LIN-3166), fixed before reading

You read one digest per ticket: its title and description head, then every comment (leg and verdict
labelled from the comment's heading) interleaved with every commit naming the ticket in either repo
(LinearViewer or simple-dispatcher). Each commit gives lines by class (prod / test / docs) and its files.
Commits marked AFTER FIRST REVIEW came after the first CODE review comment.

Every ticket here was routed LIGHT by at least one classifier, and a plan review or code review sent it
back (verdict request-changes) at least once. The question: what did the full process catch on it?

## Unit: a finding

A *finding* is one distinct problem a plan review or code review raised in a send-back (request-changes),
followed to what it changed. A finding repeated in a later round is ONE finding. Nits / notes /
non-blocking items count only if something was actually changed for them. Close-out holds count as
findings too (leg `close-out`) when the close-out refused to proceed and something changed.

For each finding record:
- `leg`: `plan-review`, `review` or `close-out`.
- `finding`: ≤ 20 words, what it said.
- `effect`: what it changed, judged from the commits and comments that followed:
  - `prod` — a production-code change (a prod-line commit the following comments tie to this finding;
    for a plan review, the plan changed AND the eventual code differs because of it in production lines)
  - `tests` — only tests, witnesses, pins, fixtures changed
  - `docs-wording` — only docs, plan text, PR/ticket/comment text changed
  - `follow-up` — filed as a separate ticket rather than fixed here
  - `nothing` — nothing traceable changed
- `realFault`: true only if, without the change, a user- or operator-visible defect (wrong behaviour,
  crash, data loss, security hole, broken contract) would have shipped on main. Missing tests, style,
  wording, scope, process-compliance and "prove it" requests are NOT real faults. If unsure, false.
- `confidence`: high / medium / low.

Also record per ticket: `sendBacks` (count of request-changes verdicts you confirm), and `note` (≤ 25 words:
what the full process bought on this ticket, in plain words; "nothing beyond evidence/wording" is a valid answer).

Output: one JSON object per ticket: {"id", "findings": [...], "sendBacks", "note"}.
